wc:
[-lwmcL] [FILE ...]
Count lines, words, characters, bytes and maximum display-line length.
Default: lines, words, bytes. -m equals -c in this byte/C-locale build.
Word/line-width rules differ from sbase Unicode handling. 32-bit counters.
tr:
[-Ccds] STRING1 [STRING2]
Translate bytes, complement (-c/-C), delete (-d), squeeze (-s).
Reads stdin, writes stdout; ASCII classes and equivalence classes enabled.
No multibyte characters or [x*N] repetition syntax.
cmp:
[-sl] [-n NUM] FILE1 [FILE2 [SKIP1 [SKIP2]]]
Compare bytes; FILE2 defaults to stdin. -s quiet, -l list differences.
Status: 0 equal, 1 different, 2 error.
sort:
[-nghucszbrdfi] [-k KEY] [-t CHAR] [FILE ...]
Sort text; numeric/general/human numeric, unique, check, stable, reverse,
NUL records, blanks/dictionary/case/unprintable filtering, field keys.
All input and keys must fit working RAM; no disk spill. C-locale ordering.
-o/-M/-V/-m/-S/-T are explicitly unsupported. Redirect to a separate file.
sed:
[-nEr] [-e SCRIPT] [-f FILE] [SCRIPT] [FILE ...]
Stream editing with addresses, substitutions, branches and hold space.
-n suppresses default output; -E/-r extended regex. Repeat -e/-f.
-i in-place editing is unavailable; redirect to a separate output file.
NUL handling follows upstream BusyBox; not a binary-transparent editor.
grep:
[-EFHhilLnqsvwxc] [-o] [-m N] [-A N] [-B N] [-C N]
       [-e PATTERN] [-f FILE] [PATTERN] [FILE ...]
Find matching lines: BRE, -E extended, -F fixed; -i ignores case.
-n numbers, -c counts, -l/-L filenames, -q quiet, -v invert.
-w words, -x whole lines, -o matching text; context via -A/-B/-C.
-r/-R recursive search unavailable. No PCRE or binary-safe GNU mode.
Status: 0 match, 1 no match, 2 error.
cat:
[FILE ...]
Copy data forks to stdout. No formatting flags in this selected build.
cut:
[-s] [-d CHAR] {-b LIST|-c LIST|-f LIST} [FILE ...]
Select bytes/characters/fields; -c is byte-oriented. -s skips lines
without delimiter. Default field delimiter TAB; LIST supports N,N-M,N-, -M.
head:
[-n N|-c N] [-qv] [FILE ...]
Print first N lines (default 10) or bytes. Negative N omits last N.
-q suppresses headers; -v always prints headers. Counts accept b/k/m suffix.
tail:
[-n N|-c N] [-qv] [FILE ...]
Print last N lines (default 10) or bytes; +N starts at N.
-q suppresses headers; -v always prints headers. Counts accept b/k/m suffix.
-f/-F/-s follow mode unavailable in this experiment.
uniq:
[-cduiz] [-f N] [-s N] [-w N] [INPUT]
Filter adjacent equal lines; -c counts, -d duplicates, -u unique,
-i ignores case, -z NUL output, -f skip fields, -s skip bytes, -w compare N.
Upstream input NUL handling has limitations. Output operand unavailable;
use shell redirection to a separate file.
tee:
[-a] [FILE ...]
Copy stdin to stdout and FILEs; -a appends. -i is explicitly unsupported:
Clarice cancellation remains enabled. Uses upstream block-I/O configuration.
cksum:
[FILE ...]
Print POSIX CRC32 and byte length. No operands reads stdin.
32-bit file length on this platform; not cryptographic authentication.
basename:
NAME [SUFFIX]
Print final slash-separated path component, optionally removing SUFFIX.
dirname:
NAME
Print slash-separated directory component using Clarice's path adapter.
